 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. CLEVELAND — The Cavaliers are hoping to build momentum coming off a feel-good win highlighted by young players' heroics while the team's regular starters sat out.
 On Monday, Nov. 16, the Cavs are receiving a chance to preserve the positive energy and move above .500 when they host the Chicago Bulls.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Cavs beat the visiting Dallas Mavericks 127-117 on Saturday, Nov. 14. The previous night, the Cavs lost 133-121 at the Miami Heat , and instead of immediately flying back to Cleveland, the team traveled home on the morning of Nov. 14 because of airline chaos created by the recent FAA ground stop.
 With coach Kenny Atkinson citing player health and care concerns, the Cavs chose to rest starting guards Donovan Mitchell and James Harden, starting center Jarrett Allen and starting wing Peyton Watson . Starting forward Evan Mobley had already been sidelined with a sprained toe.
 All five players who started for the shorthanded Cavs scored in double figures. The effort was headlined by second-year guard Tyrese Proctor's triple-double (24 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists).
 Tipoff for Cavs (7-7) versus Bulls (3-9) occurred shortly after at 7 p.m. Nov. 16 at Rocket Arena. Updates will be here throughout the game:

 The Cavaliers trailed the Bulls 31-25 at the end of the opening quarter.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Guard Buddy Hield made back-to-back 3-pointers to give the Bulls a 29-23 lead late in the first quarter.
 Donovan Mitchell responded with a high dribble and a successful floater. But on the Cavs' next two possessions, Mitchell committed a turnover with a bad pass, missed a jump shot and had the ball stolen again.
 Guard Tre Jones turned the second steal into a fast-break layup, bumping the Bulls' lead to 31-25 with five seconds left.
 The centers led the scoring — the Bulls' Jalen Smith with eight points and the Cavs' Jarrett Allen with six points.
 Cavaliers vs Bulls score tied 21-21 with 2:50 remaining in first quarter
 The Bulls have won their past two games and are apparently going to make the Cavs work. The score between the two teams was tied 21-21 during a timeout with 2:50 left in the first quarter.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Bulls are shooting 9-of-17 (52.9%) from the floor (3 of 10 on 3-pointers, 30%) thus far. The Cavs are shooting 9-of-21 (42.9%) from the field (3 of 6 on 3s, 50%).
 Score between Cavs and Bulls tied 17-17 with 7:10 left in the first quarter
 The Cavs-Bulls score was tied 17-17 during a timeout with 7:10 remaining in the opening quarter.
 Center Jarrett Allen led the Cavs with six points and two rebounds out of the gate. Bulls center Jalen Smith also had six points to go along with two assists and a rebound.

 The Cavs listed wing Peyton Watson (right abdominal soreness) as questionable before upgrading him to available. They also ruled out the following players:
 wing Jaylon Tyson (right ankle injury management)
 guard Sam Merrill (right elbow injury management)
 forward Evan Mobley (left great toe sprain)
 forward Nae'Qwan Tomin (low back stress reaction)
 center Earnest Udeh Jr. (NBA G League — two-way contract)
 Note : On Nov. 16, the Cavs announced Mobley will undergo treatment and rehabilitation over the next seven to 10 days before being reevaluated.

 The Cavs have an all-time record of 107-135 against the Bulls in the regular season.
 Will the Cleveland Cavs and Chicago Bulls meet again this season?
 The Cavs and Bulls are slated to play three more times during the 2026-27 regular season. Cleveland will visit Chicago on Nov. 23 and Dec. 3. The Bulls will play at the Cavs again on March 20.
 Where to watch Cavaliers vs Bulls tonight on TV
 Cavs versus Bulls will be televised by  DAZN , which will stream all regular-season games not selected exclusively for national broadcasts.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement How can I listen to Cavs vs Bulls tonight on radio?
 The local radio broadcast of the Cavs-Bulls game can be heard via WTAM (1100-AM), WMMS (100.7-FM) or La Mega Cleveland (Spanish broadcast, 1300-AM).
